newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 6.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's edition of The Wall Street Journal.
- Raytheon agreed to buy the missile and defense-electronics holdings of Texas Instruments for nearly $3 billion.
- Republic Industries agreed to acquire National Car Rental for $600 million in stock, plus assumption of $1.7 billion in vehicle debt.
- Apple Computer disclosed that sales of a key product line dropped significantly during the holidays, raising new doubts about a turnaround.
- The economy appears to have accelerated in the fourth quarter after slowing in the third period.
- General Motors car and light truck sales fell 14 percent in the U.S. in December.
- Disney next fall will begin allowing its animated films to be broadcast on ABC television.
- Gasoline prices should reach $1.35 per gallon this spring.
- Boehringer plans to launch its clot-busting drug Retavase to compete against Genentech s Altaplase in the heart attack treatment market.
- Fidelity Investments is losing two more managers.
- State Street Boston s chief says the bank plans to remain independent after Bank of New York said it plans to boost its stake to nearly 10 percent.
- Texaco agreed to allow the EEOC to track its employment practices.
- Beer commercials appeared during TV shows whose audiences were mostly under 21 on several occasions during one September week.
- Four Airbus partners agreed on a plan to transform the consortium into a centralized company by 1999.
- Bonds sold to finance mergers and acquisitions are once again a major part of the junk bond market after several years of relative obscurity.
